name: filter-field
title: Filter Field
description: The control for one filter schema field, named by its label: an input for text, a select or checkboxes for options, a select for a boolean, a comparison and numbers, date pickers, or a ServerCombobox for remote options.

files.content:
import type { NumberOp } from "@/lib/filter-schema"

type FilterFieldLabels = {
  /** The choice that clears a single option or a boolean. */
  any: string
  yes: string
  no: string
  from: string
  to: string
  min: string
  max: string
  value: string
  comparison: string
  operators: Record<NumberOp | "between", string>
}

const filterFieldLabels: FilterFieldLabels = {
  any: "Any",
  yes: "Yes",
  no: "No",
  from: "From",
  to: "To",
  min: "Minimum",
  max: "Maximum",
  value: "Value",
  comparison: "Comparison",
  operators: {
    eq: "Equals",
    neq: "Is not",
    lt: "Less than",
    lte: "At most",
    gt: "More than",
    gte: "At least",
    between: "Between",
  },
}

export { filterFieldLabels }
export type { FilterFieldLabels }

docs: `<FilterField field={schema.status} value onValueChange />` is controlled with the field's value type (`FilterValues`); an empty choice gives `undefined`. Options are a `Select` with Any, or a checkbox group when `multiple`; a boolean a `Select` of `trueLabel` and `falseLabel`; a number a Comparison `Select` (`operators`, `eq`, `gte`, `lte` and `between` by default) and a Value `NumberInput`, side by side once the container is 20rem wide, Minimum and Maximum for between; a date a `DatePicker`, a range two labelled From and To (each end optional); a remote option a `ServerCombobox` that says Any until something is chosen, which reports chosen labels through `onValueLabels`. `appliesAtOnce(field)` says whether a change is a pick or typing. `FilterChips` and `FilterPanel` use it; use it in a form of your own. Every control has a visible label. `labels` translates Any, Yes, No, From, To, Comparison, Value, Minimum, Maximum and the comparisons. Date pickers and number inputs take `locale`, or follow `<html lang>` through `useLocale`.
